Block is one company built from many blocks, all united by the same purpose: economic empowerment. We build technology that increases access and independence for sellers, individuals, and artists around the world. Working at Block means working on and across our brands—Square, Cash App, Afterpay, TIDAL, Spiral, and Proto— in roles that connect, enable, and push all of them forward faster.

We’re remote-first by design and operate with intelligence at the center of everything we do. At Block, you'll be challenged by some of the brightest, most creative minds in the industry and have the tools and autonomy to do the most meaningful work of your career. 

As Global Fulfillment Operations Specialist at Block, you’ll drive reliable day-to-day fulfillment of hardware across our global brands and markets. You’ll work through third-party logistics providers (3PLs) and alongside regional supplier managers to keep orders moving, resolve operational exceptions, improve inventory and shipment visibility, and strengthen the processes that connect our systems and fulfillment partners.

This individual contributor role combines hands-on operational execution, analytical problem-solving, and continuous improvement. You’ll independently own fulfillment outcomes, turning recurring issues into durable controls and scalable processes rather than repeated manual work.

Key Responsibilities

Global Fulfillment Execution & Partner Performance

  • Own fulfillment outcomes from order release through shipment confirmation for customer orders, replacements, inventory transfers, and other fulfillment flows.
  • Monitor order accuracy, processing timeliness, backlog, holds, and shipment exceptions; coordinate recovery and prioritize work within established business guidelines.
  • Drive outcomes through 3PL partners, ensuring they own their commitments rather than transferring recurring work to Block.
  • Partner with regional supplier managers on service expectations, performance reviews, capacity risks, and operational improvements.
  • Maintain clear escalation paths and cross-time-zone handoffs; support continuity and recovery during disruptions.
  • Manage actionable reporting on fulfillment performance, exceptions, and corrective actions; use data to prioritize and measure improvements.

Systems, Inventory & Operational Controls

  • Investigate order, inventory, and shipment discrepancies across systems.
  • Coordinate inventory reconciliation and resolution of interface failures, missing transactions, configuration errors, and data issues with the appropriate owners.
  • Validate system and process changes before and after implementation.
  • Maintain warehouse procedures and controls that ensure accurate execution, traceability, and reliable handoffs.

Continuous Improvement & Launch Readiness

  • Identify recurring failures and manual work; eliminate, automate, or simplify them through root-cause improvements.
  • Independently lead defined improvement initiatives through implementation and measured results.
  • Build standard work, self-service resources, and exception-management processes that reduce individual intervention.
  • Enable product launches, new markets and channels, and warehouse or system transitions by testing fulfillment flows and closing readiness gaps.

Supplier Cost Management & Billing Controls

  • Validate fulfillment supplier invoices against contracted rates, actual activity, and approved charges; resolve discrepancies and track credits through closure.
  • Monitor spend and cost per order, investigate variances, and identify savings opportunities without compromising service.
  • Partner with supplier managers and Finance to improve billing accuracy, cost reporting, and automated controls that prevent recurring errors.

Qualifications

Required Experience & Skills

  • 5+ years of relevant experience in fulfillment, order management, warehouse operations, logistics, or supply chain, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Practical knowledge of ERP, order-management, and warehouse-management systems, including investigating transaction and inventory discrepancies.
  • Strong analytical skills and proficiency with driving controls through operational reporting.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage operational workflows, resolve exceptions, and deliver defined improvement projects.
  • Ability to identify root causes and build repeatable solutions rather than rely on recurring manual intervention
  • Ability to influence internal stakeholders and external partners without direct authority.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Oracle or comparable ERP platforms.
  • Experience supporting global hardware fulfillment across direct-to-consumer, retail, or business-to-business channels.
  • Familiarity with integrations between ERP, order-management, and 3PL warehouse systems.
  • Experience building dashboards, automated reporting, or workflow automation.
  • Experience supporting product launches, warehouse transitions, or fulfillment-system changes.
  • Working knowledge of international logistics and the handoffs between fulfillment, freight, and trade compliance.

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Fraud Architect team helps Stripe’s largest and most complex users manage fraud and abuse across the customer lifecycle. We combine deep fraud expertise, technical investigation, and product knowledge to help users understand emerging threats, optimize Radar, and implement durable prevention strategies tailored to their business and risk tolerance. Our goal is to enable users’ growth by proactively reducing fraud while protecting legitimate customer activity and turning frontline insights into better products and defenses.

What you’ll do

Stripe users face fraud and abuse across the customer lifecycle, including payment fraud, free-trial farming, multi-account abuse, and usage-based billing exploitation. They need a partner who understands their business, anticipates emerging threats, and helps them put effective protections in place as their business and the threat landscape evolve.

As a member of our Fraud Architect team, you’ll be the fraud and risk specialist embedded in strategic user relationships for a small portfolio of named users, acting as a technical extension of their teams. You’ll help users get more from Radar, build a proactive prevention strategy, and turn complex fraud problems into practical decisions.

This role combines analytical rigor, deep fraud investigation, and product judgment. You’ll develop a deep understanding of how Radar scores and classifies transactions, how integrations and available signals affect its decisions, and where its capabilities and limitations matter for a user. You’ll explain what the evidence supports, investigate what it does not yet explain, and translate both into action: better rules and thresholds, integration guidance, or model and feature gaps to pursue with our product teams.

Your focus is proactive, user-specific risk ownership and durable prevention. You’ll provide user context, communicate implications and next steps, and turn incident findings into an implemented and verified prevention plan. You’ll help build, expand, and evolve defenses as user needs and fraud patterns change.

Responsibilities

  • Own each user’s prevention strategy. Maintain a current risk baseline, threat model, and agreed prevention plan for every assigned account. Understand payment methods, integrations, billing flows, trial and promotion mechanics, existing controls, and risk preferences; identify the top risks and gaps across the full customer lifecycle.
  • Make Radar’s behavior understandable and actionable. Investigate scoring, classification, rule behavior, and signal coverage using transaction evidence and technical context. Explain observed behavior and uncertainty clearly, distinguish configuration or integration issues from potential model or feature gaps, and recommend the right next step for the user and our product teams.
  • Design and improve user protections. Help users configure and optimize Radar for their business model and risk tolerance. Training

What You’ll Do

  • Be the voice of Ramp's Customer Support. You'll spend your day engaging with customers, primarily via live calls, email, and chat.

You'll work across Zendesk, internal tooling, and Slack-based escalation workflows.

  • Build and shape AI tools, not just use them. Ramp is building AI into CX operations. You'll use AI-powered research tools and proprietary tools like Glass daily, provide direct feedback on what's working, and play an active role in how these tools evolve.   • Ship improvements, not just flag them.   • Communicate with precision and empathy. Our customers are financially sophisticated. You need to explain what's happening, what you're doing about it, and what they should expect — clearly and without filler.

What You Need

  • You're a systems thinker: you don't just solve the ticket in front of you, you ask why the problem exists and how to prevent it from happening again.

  • You actively use AI tools — Claude, Notion AI, research and workflow tools — and can demonstrate how you've applied them to get real work done. This is a hard requirement.

  • You're fast-moving while holding yourself to a high bar for execution: you balance speed, accuracy, and thoroughness in every interaction.

  • You're comfortable on the phone. Many interactions start there.

  • You have a demonstrated track record of exceeding key performance standards, including CSAT, QA, and speed-of-service metrics.

  • Experience building workflows or automations using AI tools, not just prompting

  • Familiarity with accounting workflows (AP/AR, GL, reconciliation) or ERP integrations (NetSuite, QuickBooks, Sage)

  • Background in payments infrastructure (ACH, wire transfers, card networks)

  • Track record of working somewhere that shipped product fast and expected CX to keep up

Why be a CX Associate at Ramp

  • Cross-functional exposure from day one. You work directly with Product, Engineering, and GTM teams — not siloed into a support queue.

  • AI tools and unlimited access. Unlimited tokens, proprietary AI tools like Glass, and a culture that expects you to use them to move faster and build smarter.

  • Career growth that you own. Grow within CX, explore other functions internally, or carve out a path that doesn't exist yet. If you're invested, we're invested.

  • Culture that's different from a call center. Team events, in-person offsites, and a genuine commitment to building a team people want to be part of.
